typeset.typ

The Typst implementation. Same specification, different engine — and Typst does the things CSS cannot: page-foot footnotes, running heads, and table-of-contents page numbers, all natively.

Typst needs the font files themselves. Unlike CSS there is no URL to point at: a font is either in the project or it is not, and a missing family is substituted silently. So this one ships as a bundle — the implementation, all three example documents, and the three font families the spec names, licences included.

Compile with typst compile --font-path fonts implementations/example-essay.typ out.pdf, or drag the unzipped folder into a typst.app project.

The bundle is built from this repository on every deploy, so it can never drift from the fonts and implementation above.

1// typeset — Typst implementation of https://typeset.adilsoncarvalho.com
2//
3// The normative source is spec.json. Every value below is taken from it. Where
4// this file and the spec disagree, the spec is right.
5//
6// Usage:
7// #import "typeset.typ": *
8// #show: typeset
9//
10// Every name this file defines is a name a document may need, so the import is
11// a star import: a hand-picked list silently denies whichever name the next
12// document reaches for, and the failure reads as "unknown variable" rather than
13// as a missing import.
14//
15// typeset() takes the document's options — paper, margin, justified, indented,
16// numbered, measure and the rest, declared below. A document that sets any of
17// them writes `#show: typeset.with(...)` in place of the bare `#show: typeset`
18// above, never underneath it: typeset() sets the page, and set page() is
19// refused inside a container, which is what a second call would make of the
20// first. So a document on another paper, at another margin, opens with
21// `#show: typeset.with(paper: "a5", margin: margin-narrow)` and nothing else.
22
23// ── Foundation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
24
25// @s tokens
26#let ink = rgb("#1a1a1a")
27#let ink-muted = rgb("#5a5a5a")
28#let ink-faint = rgb("#8a8a8a")
29#let rule-color = rgb("#c9c4bd")
30#let rule-strong = rgb("#6f6a64")
31#let wash = rgb("#f4f1ec")
32#let accent = rgb("#7a1f1f")
33
34#let serif = "EB Garamond"
35#let sans = "Source Sans 3"
36#let mono = "IBM Plex Mono"
37
38// A template supplies one of these. Every size in the document comes from it,
39// so nothing downstream has to know which template is in force.
40#let scale-single-column = (
41 xs: 8pt, sm: 9.5pt, base: 11pt,
42 h4: 12pt, h3: 14pt, h2: 18pt, h1: 24pt,
43 leading: 1.45, space: 11pt,
44)
45
46// Two columns: every step comes down. On A4 at the standard margin an 82mm
47// column carries 42 characters at 11pt — below the 45-character floor — so the
48// base drops to 9.5pt, which gives 49.
49#let scale-two-column = (
50 xs: 7pt, sm: 8.5pt, base: 9.5pt,
51 h4: 9.5pt, h3: 11pt, h2: 13pt, h1: 20pt,
52 leading: 1.4, space: 9.5pt,
53)
54
55// Defaults, for the standalone helpers below.
56#let base-size = scale-single-column.base
57#let sm = scale-single-column.sm
58#let xs = scale-single-column.xs
59
60// One unit of vertical space: 11pt, one line of base leading.
61#let sp = 11pt
62
63// The spec states line height as a baseline-to-baseline advance. Typst measures
64// leading between line boxes, so pinning the box to the band from the baseline
65// up to 1em makes the advance font-independent:
66// advance = top-edge - bottom-edge + leading = 1em + leading
67// so leading = (line_height - 1) em. 1.45 → 0.45em → 15.95pt at 11pt.
68#let leading-for(line-height) = (line-height - 1) * 1em
69
70// Paragraph separation is one decision expressed as two par properties, never
71// both at once: a gap (spaced) or an indent (indented). `typeset()`'s own
72// `indented` option and the two standalone functions below (block-spaced,
73// block-indented) both read this, so the whole-document switch and the
74// per-block override can never drift apart into two different 1.5em's.
75// `leading` defaults to the single-column scale's own 1.45 for the two
76// standalone functions, which have no `scale` to read; typeset() passes its
77// own scale's leading, so a document on the two-column scale still gets
78// indented spacing equal to ITS leading, not the single-column one's.
79#let _paragraphs-rule(indented, leading: 1.45) = if indented {
80 (spacing: leading-for(leading), first-line-indent: (amount: 1.5em, all: false))
81} else {
82 (spacing: sp, first-line-indent: 0pt)
83}
84
85#let oldstyle = (number-type: "old-style", number-width: "proportional")
86#let lining = (number-type: "lining", number-width: "proportional")
87#let tabular = (number-type: "lining", number-width: "tabular")
88// @e
89#let smcp = (features: ("smcp", "c2sc"))
90
91// ── Page ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
92
93// Paper and margin are independent choices. A margin is millimetres, and the
94// same millimetres on every paper, so
95// #show: typeset.with(paper: "a5", margin: margin-narrow)
96// asks for both without either one knowing about the other.
97//
98// Symmetric is what a document gets unless it asks otherwise: the named size
99// on all four sides. Duplex is the opt-in for a sheet that will be bound — top
100// and bottom keep the symmetric value, and the sides split into an inner
101// (binding) edge and an outer one, which Typst mirrors by page parity. Each
102// duplex pair sums to twice its symmetric value, so a document keeps the same
103// text width, and the same line breaks, whichever of the two it chooses.
104//
105// The prefix names the family, matching typeset.css's `typeset--margin-narrow`.
106// `narrow` and `wide` also name measure variants, which are a different axis:
107// one word must not reach both.
108#let margin-narrow = (top: 10mm, bottom: 10mm, left: 10mm, right: 10mm)
109#let margin-standard = (top: 20mm, bottom: 20mm, left: 20mm, right: 20mm)
110#let margin-wide = (top: 30mm, bottom: 30mm, left: 30mm, right: 30mm)
111
112#let margin-duplex-narrow = (top: 10mm, bottom: 10mm, inside: 13mm, outside: 7mm)
113#let margin-duplex-standard = (top: 20mm, bottom: 20mm, inside: 23mm, outside: 17mm)
114#let margin-duplex-wide = (top: 30mm, bottom: 30mm, inside: 33mm, outside: 27mm)
115
116// The numbers stay reachable behind the names: `margin` takes any length or
117// any Typst margin dictionary, so `margin: 18mm` is there for a printer who
118// needs a measurement rather than a name.
119
120// Every paper this spec is set for, width before height, under the name Typst
121// knows it by — "us-letter" is the spec's Letter. The two-column derivation is
122// arithmetic on this table, so a paper reaches that arithmetic by being added
123// here.
124#let paper-sizes-mm = (
125 "a4": (210mm, 297mm),
126 "a5": (148mm, 210mm),
127 "us-letter": (215.9mm, 279.4mm),
128)
129
130// The measure — one column's ideal line length. Three named widths, matching
131// typeset.css's own three measure classes: standard is the default, narrow
132// and wide are the modifiers a document opts into. All three are em, the
133// axis spec.json states them in and typeset.css already uses; an em measure
134// follows a scale change, where an mm one would not.
135#let measure-standard = 33em
136#let measure-narrow = 27em
137#let measure-wide = 40em
138
139// The fourth width, and the only one with no spec.json literal behind it:
140// the full text block, derived from the default paper and margin above
141// rather than typed. A4 at the standard margin leaves 170mm between the
142// margins.
143#let measure-full = paper-sizes-mm.at("a4").at(0) - 2 * margin-standard.left
144
145// A document reaches for one of the four names instead of a literal width:
146// `#measured[...]` for the default column, `#measured(width:
147// measure-wide)[...]` for a modifier, `#measured(width: measure-full)[...]`
148// for the full text block.
149#let measured(width: measure-standard, body) = block(width: width, body)
150
151// ── Document ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
152
153#let typeset(
154 // The paper by its Typst name, and the margin by one of the six names above
155 // — or by any length, for a page box the spec does not name.
156 paper: "a4",
157 margin: margin-standard,
158 scale: scale-single-column,
159 // Ragged right is the default. Justification buys a clean right edge at the
160 // cost of uneven word spacing; choose it for continuous prose at a full
161 // measure, and leave it off for a letter or a note addressed to a person.
162 justified: false,
163 indented: false,
164 numbered: false,
165 running-head: true,
166 folio: true,
167 // The measure, not the text width. A4 at the standard margin leaves
168 // measure-full (170mm) between its margins; measure-standard is smaller
169 // and keeps the remainder as slack, which is where marginalia live. It is
170 // a maximum, so a page with less than measure-standard between its
171 // margins keeps its margins. Pass `none` where the column IS the measure,
172 // as in two columns.
173 measure: measure-standard,
174 doc,
175) = {
176 let sm = scale.sm
177 let xs = scale.xs
178 let sp = scale.space
179// @s page
180 set page(
181 paper: paper,
182 margin: margin,
183 header: context {
184 // The running head follows the current level-2 heading, and is
185 // suppressed on the opening page.
186 if running-head and here().page() > 1 {
187 let seen = query(selector(heading.where(level: 2)).before(here()))
188 if seen.len() > 0 {
189 set text(font: sans, size: xs, fill: ink-faint, tracking: 0.08em)
190 align(center, upper(seen.last().body))
191 }
192 }
193 },
194 footer: context {
195 if folio and here().page() > 1 {
196 set text(font: serif, size: 9pt, fill: ink-muted, ..oldstyle)
197 align(center, counter(page).display())
198 }
199 },
200// @e
201 )
202
203// @s foundation
204 set text(
205 font: serif,
206 size: scale.base,
207 fill: ink,
208 top-edge: 1em,
209 bottom-edge: 0pt,
210 ..oldstyle,
211 )
212
213 set par(
214 leading: leading-for(scale.leading),
215 .._paragraphs-rule(indented, leading: scale.leading),
216 justify: justified,
217// @e
218 linebreaks: "optimized",
219 )
220
221 // Hyphenation is per-language and only ever paired with justification.
222 set text(hyphenate: justified)
223
224 // Widow and orphan control: never one line alone at a page edge.
225 set block(breakable: true)
226
227 set heading(numbering: if numbered { "1.1 " } else { none })
228
229 // ── Headings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
230 // Space above is four times the space below; a heading belongs to what
231 // follows it. `sticky` is Typst's break-after: avoid.
232
233// @s headings
234 show heading: set text(font: sans, hyphenate: false)
235 show heading: set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
236 show heading: it => block(
237 above: sp * 2,
238 below: sp * 0.5,
239 sticky: true,
240 breakable: false,
241 it,
242 )
243
244 show heading.where(level: 1): set text(size: scale.h1, weight: 300, tracking: -0.015em)
245 show heading.where(level: 1): it => block(above: 0pt, below: sp * 0.5, sticky: true, it)
246 show heading.where(level: 2): set text(size: scale.h2, weight: 600, tracking: -0.01em)
247 show heading.where(level: 3): set text(size: scale.h3, weight: 600)
248 show heading.where(level: 4): set text(size: scale.h4, weight: 600)
249 show heading.where(level: 5): set text(
250 font: serif, size: scale.base, weight: 600, tracking: 0.06em, ..smcp,
251 )
252 show heading.where(level: 6): set text(
253// @e
254 font: serif, size: scale.base, weight: 400, style: "italic",
255 )
256
257 // ── Quotations ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
258
259// @s quotes
260 show quote.where(block: true): it => block(
261 above: sp * 1.25,
262 below: sp * 1.25,
263 inset: (left: sp * 1.5),
264 stroke: (left: 1pt + rule-color),
265 breakable: false,
266 {
267 set text(size: 0.955em)
268 it.body
269 if it.attribution != none {
270 set text(size: sm, fill: ink-muted, style: "normal")
271 set par(first-line-indent: 0pt, justify: false)
272 block(above: sp * 0.5, [— #it.attribution])
273 }
274 },
275 )
276
277// @e
278 // ── Lists ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
279
280// @s lists
281 set list(marker: ([#text(fill: ink-muted, weight: 700)[·]], [#text(fill: ink-muted)[–]]), indent: 0pt, body-indent: 1.4em, spacing: sp * 0.25)
282 set enum(numbering: "1.", indent: 0pt, body-indent: 1.4em, spacing: sp * 0.25, number-align: left)
283 show enum: set text(..tabular)
284
285 set terms(separator: linebreak(), indent: 0pt, hanging-indent: sp * 1.5, spacing: sp * 0.6)
286 show terms: set par(first-line-indent: 0pt)
287 show terms.item: it => block(above: sp * 0.6, below: 0pt, {
288 block(below: 0pt, text(font: sans, size: sm, weight: 600, it.term))
289 block(inset: (left: sp * 1.5), it.description)
290 })
291
292// @e
293 // ── Tables ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
294 // Rules, not grids: a rule above the header, below the header, below the body.
295
296// @s tables
297 set table(
298 stroke: (x, y) => (bottom: if y == 0 { 1pt + rule-strong } else { 0.5pt + rule-color }),
299 inset: (left: 0pt, right: 0.7em, top: 0.45em, bottom: 0.45em),
300 align: left + horizon,
301 )
302 show table: set text(font: sans, size: sm, ..tabular)
303 show table: set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.35), first-line-indent: 0pt)
304 show table.cell.where(y: 0): set text(size: xs, weight: 600, fill: ink-muted, tracking: 0.07em)
305 show table.cell.where(y: 0): upper
306
307// @e
308 // ── Figures & captions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
309
310// @s figures
311 show figure: set block(above: sp * 1.5, below: sp * 1.5, breakable: false)
312 show figure.caption: it => block(
313 width: 100%,
314 inset: (top: 0.4em),
315 stroke: (top: 0.5pt + rule-color),
316 {
317 set text(font: sans, size: sm, fill: ink-muted)
318 set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.4), first-line-indent: 0pt)
319 align(left, [#text(fill: ink, weight: 600, tracking: 0.06em, ..smcp)[#it.supplement #context it.counter.display()] — #it.body])
320 },
321 )
322
323// @e
324 // ── Code ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
325
326// @s codeblock
327 show raw: set text(font: mono, size: 0.86em, features: (liga: 0))
328 show raw.where(block: false): box.with(fill: wash, inset: (x: 0.28em), outset: (y: 0.1em), radius: 2pt)
329 show raw.where(block: true): it => block(
330 width: 100%,
331 fill: wash,
332 stroke: (left: 2pt + rule-strong),
333 inset: (x: 1em, y: 0.8em),
334 above: sp * 1.25,
335 below: sp * 1.25,
336 breakable: true,
337 { set text(size: 0.773em); set par(leading: leading-for(1.45), justify: false); it },
338 )
339
340// @e
341 // ── Inline ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
342
343// @s inline
344 show strong: set text(weight: 600)
345 show link: it => underline(offset: 0.14em, stroke: 0.5pt, it)
346 show footnote: set text(fill: accent, size: 0.7em, ..lining)
347 set footnote.entry(separator: line(length: 30%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule-color))
348 show footnote.entry: set text(size: sm)
349
350// @e
351
352 // Running heads and folios still span the full text width; only the flow is
353 // constrained. The block is breakable, so pagination is unaffected. The width
354 // is taken against the page actually in force rather than against A4, and the
355 // measure is resolved to absolute units first, because it is as often given
356 // in ems as in millimetres.
357 if measure == none { doc } else {
358 layout(size => context {
359 block(width: calc.min(measure.to-absolute(), size.width), doc)
360 })
361 }
362}
363
364// ── Paragraphs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
365
366// `typeset()`'s own `indented` option applies one of these two to the whole
367// document. These exist for the one block that needs the OTHER convention —
368// the same reason `justified`/`ragged-right` exist for alignment. Spaced is
369// the document default and so needs no wrapper of its own for that reason,
370// but it still gets one: the way back, for one block, in a document set to
371// indented.
372//
373// Named for what they do to the reader's block, not for the spec's own
374// paragraphs-spaced/paragraphs-indented element ids: an author reaching for
375// one of these is asking "how does this block behave", never "which section
376// of the specification is this" — and a name tied to the element id would
377// also have to change the day that id does.
378//
379// `first-line-indent`'s `all: false` is what makes indented prose behave:
380// Typst withholds the indent from a paragraph that opens the document, and
381// from one right after a heading, a blockquote, a figure or a break, because
382// each of those is itself a block and a block resets the same state a
383// document start does. A `block()` wrapper here would do that AGAIN to the
384// first paragraph *inside* this function — flushing a paragraph that is not
385// actually after a heading, a bug this file's own conformance gate compiles
386// a probe to catch. So `body` below is scoped by a plain code block, which
387// carries no layout identity of its own, never by `block()`.
388// @s paragraphs
389#let block-spaced(body) = {
390 set par(.._paragraphs-rule(false))
391 body
392}
393
394#let block-indented(body) = {
395 set par(.._paragraphs-rule(true))
396 body
397}
398// @e
399
400// ── Alignment ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
401
402// Ragged right is `typeset()`'s own document-wide default (its `justified`
403// option). These two exist for the one paragraph, list item, blockquote or
404// callout that needs the OTHER convention, so an author reaches for a name
405// instead of `#set par(justify: ..)` and `#set text(hyphenate: ..)` by hand —
406// the same reason block-spaced/block-indented exist for paragraph spacing.
407//
408// Justification and hyphenation are a single decision, never two: hyphenate
409// is never a parameter here, only `lang`, because hyphenation is per-language
410// and requires the document language to be declared. `justified(lang: none)`
411// is how a document states that no dictionary is declared for this block —
412// honestly, not as a footgun to avoid, since that combination (justified,
413// unhyphenated) is exactly what opens rivers of white space down the page.
414// `ragged-right` takes the same `lang` parameter for the language-sensitive
415// typesetting `hyphenate` is not (quotation marks, spacing rules) — but never
416// hyphenates, `lang` or not: a hyphen exists to serve justification, and
417// breaks a word for no gain without it.
418//
419// `set align(left)` is not restating the ambient default. Alignment inherits,
420// and Typst resolves a justified paragraph's last line against that same
421// inherited alignment — so a block nested inside a centred or right-aligned
422// context that only set `justify` would flush its last line, or its only
423// line for a one-liner, to whatever alignment surrounds it, correct only
424// where that happens to already be left. Stating `align(left)` here is what
425// makes both functions' own alignment, and their own last-line alignment,
426// hold regardless of where they are nested — never true "by inheritance"
427// alone.
428//
429// Typst's `text()` exposes only `hyphenate: bool`, with no per-language
430// tuning surface — no parameter takes justification-justified's own
431// hyphenation_min_word_chars (6), hyphenation_min_chars_before_break (3),
432// hyphenation_min_chars_after_break (3) or max_consecutive_hyphens (2).
433// typeset.css enforces those same four numbers with `hyphenate-limit-chars`
434// and `hyphenate-limit-lines`; there is no Typst engine feature this file can
435// set in their place.
436// @s justification
437#let ragged-right(indented: false, lang: "en", body) = {
438 set align(left)
439 set par(.._paragraphs-rule(indented), justify: false)
440 if lang != none { set text(lang: lang) }
441 set text(hyphenate: false)
442 body
443}
444
445#let justified(indented: false, lang: "en", body) = {
446 set align(left)
447 set par(.._paragraphs-rule(indented), justify: true)
448 if lang != none { set text(lang: lang) }
449 set text(hyphenate: lang != none)
450 body
451}
452// @e
453
454// ── Blocks the spec names but no engine provides ────────────────────────────
455
456#let quotes-epigraph(attribution: none, body) = context {
457 let u = text.size
458 block(above: 0pt, below: u * 2, width: 24em, {
459 set align(left)
460 set text(size: u * 0.91, style: "italic", fill: ink-muted)
461 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
462 body
463 if attribution != none {
464 block(above: u * 0.5, text(style: "normal", size: u * 0.86)[— #attribution])
465 }
466 })
467}
468#let epigraph-right(attribution: none, body) = align(right, quotes-epigraph(attribution: attribution, body))
469
470#let quotes-pullquote(body) = context {
471 let u = text.size
472 block(
473 above: u * 1.5, below: u * 1.5, width: 100%,
474 inset: (y: u),
475 stroke: (top: 1.5pt + rule-strong, bottom: 0.5pt + rule-color),
476 {
477 set text(font: sans, size: u * 1.36, weight: 300)
478 set par(leading: leading-for(1.3), justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
479 align(center, body)
480 },
481 )
482}
483
484#let quotes-verse(body) = block(
485 above: sp * 1.25, below: sp * 1.25,
486 inset: (left: sp * 2),
487 {
488 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt, hanging-indent: 1.5em)
489 body
490 },
491)
492
493// @s callouts
494#let callouts-callout(title: none, warning: false, body) = context {
495 let u = text.size
496 block(
497 above: u * 1.25, below: u * 1.25, width: 100%,
498 fill: wash,
499 stroke: (
500 rest: 0.5pt + rule-color,
501 left: 2.5pt + (if warning { accent } else { rule-strong }),
502 ),
503 inset: (x: 1em, y: 0.75em),
504 breakable: false,
505 {
506 set text(size: u * 0.91)
507 if title != none {
508 block(below: 0.35em, text(
509 font: sans, size: u * 0.73, weight: 700, tracking: 0.09em,
510 fill: if warning { accent } else { ink-muted },
511 upper(title),
512 ))
513 }
514 body
515 },
516 )
517}
518// @e
519
520// Section breaks. A blank line cannot survive a page break, so the mark is
521// always visible. The spec names four registers, so there are four symbols
522// here — a caller should not have to know a string literal to pick one.
523// @s breaks
524#let _break-mark(mark, size: 10pt, tracking: 0em, color: ink-faint) = block(
525 above: sp * 1.5, below: sp * 1.5, sticky: true, width: 100%,
526 align(center, box(text(size: size, fill: color, tracking: tracking, mark))),
527)
528
529#let breaks-asterisks() = _break-mark([\* \* \*], tracking: 0.6em)
530#let breaks-asterism() = _break-mark([⁂], size: 14pt)
531#let breaks-fleuron() = _break-mark([❦], size: 12pt, color: accent)
532#let breaks-rule() = block(above: sp * 1.5, below: sp * 1.5, sticky: true, width: 100%,
533 align(center, line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule-color)))
534// @e
535
536// Drop cap. Typst has no float, so the spec's three-line wrap is NOT
537// expressible here: text cannot flow around a raised initial. Two honest
538// options, and one trap:
539// * `dropcap` below sets the initial in the margin — a marginal initial. The
540// measure stays intact and the opening still gets its signal.
541// * The `droplet` package implements a true wrap by measuring lines. Use it
542// where the three-line wrap is required rather than approximated.
543// * Do NOT put the cap and the paragraph in a two-column grid: that narrows
544// the entire opening paragraph, not just its first three lines.
545// @s dropcap
546#let dropcap(body) = {
547 let letters = body.text
548 let initial = letters.first()
549 let rest = letters.slice(1)
550 block(above: 0pt, {
551 place(
552 left,
553 dx: -1.35em,
554 dy: -0.08em,
555 text(size: 3.05em, fill: accent, top-edge: "cap-height", bottom-edge: "baseline")[#initial],
556 )
557 par(first-line-indent: 0pt)[#rest]
558 })
559}
560// @e
561
562// A table that fills the measure and closes with a strong rule. Typst's stroke
563// function cannot see the row count, so it is passed in.
564#let ts-table(columns: none, rows: none, ..cells) = {
565 table(
566 columns: columns,
567 stroke: (x, y) => (bottom: if y == 0 or y == rows { 1pt + rule-strong } else { 0.5pt + rule-color }),
568 ..cells,
569 )
570}
571
572// @s two-column
573// Two columns, equal. Papers, journal articles, newsletters, technical notes.
574//
575// `front` is set full width before the columns begin — a title block, an
576// abstract, a level-1 heading. Everything in `doc` flows in two columns.
577//
578// Typst's own `page(columns: 2)` fixes the gutter at 4% of the page width
579// (8.4mm on A4). The spec says 6mm, so the body goes through `columns()`
580// instead, which takes an explicit gutter and still breaks across pages.
581
582// Whether the content being laid out right now is the two-column body (inside
583// `columns()`), as opposed to `front` or a single-column template — read by
584// frontmatter-title-block, frontmatter-abstract and frontmatter-colophon to
585// decide whether they need to promote themselves.
586#let ts-two-column-body = state("ts-two-column-body", false)
587
588// Promotes body content to a parent-scoped float spanning both columns. A
589// spanning element costs a break in both, so it is opt-in per instance for
590// spanning.optional content (figure, table, code block, pull quote) and must
591// sit at the top or the bottom of the page — never mid-column, which makes
592// the reader find their place twice.
593#let span(body, at-bottom: false) = place(
594 if at-bottom { bottom } else { top },
595 scope: "parent",
596 float: true,
597 block(width: 100%, body),
598)
599
600#let two-column(
601 paper: "a4",
602 margin: margin-standard,
603 front: none,
604 column-rule: false,
605 justified: true,
606 numbered: false,
607 running-head: true,
608 folio: true,
609 doc,
610) = {
611 // The gutter is the one number this template chooses. The column, the
612 // character count and the decision to set at all are functions of the paper
613 // and the margin, recomputed here rather than carried as a list of papers
614 // that work.
615 let gutter = 6mm
616 let floor = 45
617 let base = scale-two-column.base
618
619 // The foundation measure is 66 characters in 128mm at 11pt. Characters in a
620 // column follow from it, by the column's width and by the base in use.
621 let chars-in = width => int(calc.round(66 / 128 * (width / 1mm) * (11pt / base)))
622 let mm-of = value => {
623 let n = calc.round(value / 1mm, digits: 2)
624 if n == calc.round(n) { str(int(n)) } else { str(n) }
625 }
626
627 let size = paper-sizes-mm.at(lower(paper), default: none)
628 if size == none {
629 panic("two columns are derived from the paper's width, and \"" + paper
630 + "\" is not a paper this spec is set for: "
631 + paper-sizes-mm.keys().join(", "))
632 }
633
634 // The margin arrives as one of the six names, as a length, or as any Typst
635 // margin dictionary. The column needs the two horizontal sides; the optional
636 // rule needs all four.
637 let sides = if type(margin) == dictionary {
638 let rest = margin.at("rest", default: none)
639 let x = margin.at("x", default: rest)
640 let y = margin.at("y", default: rest)
641 (
642 top: margin.at("top", default: y),
643 bottom: margin.at("bottom", default: y),
644 inner: margin.at("inside", default: margin.at("left", default: x)),
645 outer: margin.at("outside", default: margin.at("right", default: x)),
646 )
647 } else {
648 (top: margin, bottom: margin, inner: margin, outer: margin)
649 }
650 for (side, value) in sides {
651 if type(value) != length {
652 panic("two columns are derived from the margin in millimetres, and `margin` gives "
653 + side + " as " + repr(value))
654 }
655 }
656
657 let text-width = size.at(0) - sides.inner - sides.outer
658 let column = (text-width - gutter) / 2
659 let chars = chars-in(column)
660
661 // Refused, not set badly. A column below the floor is a measure this spec
662 // does not allow, and the numbers that produced it belong in the message:
663 // the paper, the margin, the column, the count, the floor.
664 if chars < floor {
665 let named = (
666 ("narrow", margin-narrow),
667 ("standard", margin-standard),
668 ("wide", margin-wide),
669 ("duplex-narrow", margin-duplex-narrow),
670 ("duplex-standard", margin-duplex-standard),
671 ("duplex-wide", margin-duplex-wide),
672 )
673 let this-margin = "a " + mm-of(sides.inner) + "mm and " + mm-of(sides.outer) + "mm margin"
674 for (name, value) in named {
675 if margin == value { this-margin = "the " + name + " margin" }
676 }
677 // Which margins do reach the floor on this paper. A duplex pair has its
678 // symmetric pair's total, so it reaches exactly where that one does.
679 let reaching = ()
680 for (name, value) in (("narrow", margin-narrow), ("standard", margin-standard), ("wide", margin-wide)) {
681 if chars-in((size.at(0) - value.left - value.right - gutter) / 2) >= floor {
682 reaching.push(name)
683 }
684 }
685 let alternatives = if reaching.len() > 0 {
686 reaching.join(" and ") + " reach it on this paper"
687 } else {
688 "no named margin reaches it — " + upper(paper) + " cannot carry two columns at " + repr(base)
689 }
690 panic("two columns are refused on " + upper(paper) + " at " + this-margin + " — "
691 + mm-of(size.at(0)) + "mm of paper less " + mm-of(sides.inner) + "mm and "
692 + mm-of(sides.outer) + "mm leaves " + mm-of(text-width) + "mm of text, so a column is ("
693 + mm-of(text-width) + " - " + mm-of(gutter) + ") / 2 = " + mm-of(column)
694 + "mm, carrying " + str(chars) + " characters at " + repr(base) + ", below the "
695 + str(floor) + "-character floor; " + alternatives)
696 }
697
698 // Justification is not optional at a column measure.
699 assert(justified, message: "two-column requires justification: at " + str(chars)
700 + " characters a ragged edge serrates the column")
701
702 show: typeset.with(
703 paper: paper,
704 margin: margin,
705 scale: scale-two-column,
706 measure: none, // the column is the measure
707 justified: true,
708 indented: true, // a blank line costs 3% of a column
709 numbered: numbered,
710 running-head: running-head,
711 folio: folio,
712 )
713
714 // A hairline where the columns need separating. Most journals omit it — the
715 // gutter is already doing the work. `columns()` has no rule of its own, so it
716 // is drawn on the page behind the text, at the centre of the gutter. The
717 // offset flips with page parity because a duplex margin puts the inner edge
718 // on the left of an odd page and on the right of an even one.
719 //
720 // The set rule is unconditional, with the condition inside its argument, and
721 // it comes before any content: a set rule inside an `if` block applies only
722 // within that block, which holds no content, and a page set rule that follows
723 // content starts a new page.
724 set page(background: if column-rule {
725 context {
726 let left-margin = if calc.odd(here().page()) { sides.inner } else { sides.outer }
727 place(
728 top + left,
729 dx: left-margin + column + gutter / 2,
730 dy: sides.top,
731 line(
732 angle: 90deg,
733 length: size.at(1) - sides.top - sides.bottom,
734 stroke: 0.5pt + rule-color,
735 ),
736 )
737 }
738 })
739
740 if front != none {
741 front
742 v(scale-two-column.space, weak: true)
743 }
744
745 // templates.two-column.spanning.always spans without a mark from here on:
746 // frontmatter-title-block, frontmatter-abstract and frontmatter-colophon
747 // read ts-two-column-body themselves (it carries subtitle, byline and
748 // dateline too — they are that block's own parameters, not standalone
749 // functions), and a body-level level-1 heading is promoted by the show rule
750 // below. Both are scoped to `doc`; `front` above renders before the columns
751 // begin, so it is already full width and never needs the wrap.
752 ts-two-column-body.update(true)
753 show heading.where(level: 1): it => span(it)
754 columns(2, gutter: gutter, doc)
755}
756// @e
757
758// ── Front matter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
759
760// @s frontmatter
761#let frontmatter-title-block(title: none, subtitle: none, author: none, place-date: none) = context {
762 let u = text.size
763 let content = block(
764 below: u * 3, width: 100%,
765 inset: (bottom: u),
766 stroke: (bottom: 0.5pt + rule-color),
767 {
768 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
769 if title != none { heading(level: 1, outlined: false, title) }
770 if subtitle != none {
771 block(below: u, text(font: sans, size: u * 1.27, weight: 300, fill: ink-muted, subtitle))
772 }
773 if author != none { text(tracking: 0.08em, ..smcp, author) }
774 if place-date != none {
775 block(above: 0.2em, text(font: sans, size: u * 0.86, fill: ink-muted, place-date))
776 }
777 },
778 )
779 if ts-two-column-body.get() { span(content) } else { content }
780}
781// @e
782
783#let frontmatter-abstract(width: 30em, body) = context {
784 let u = text.size
785 let content = block(below: u * 2, width: width, {
786 set text(size: u * 0.91, fill: ink-muted)
787 set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.45), first-line-indent: 0pt)
788 block(below: 0.3em, text(font: sans, size: u * 0.73, weight: 700, tracking: 0.1em, fill: ink-faint)[ABSTRACT])
789 body
790 })
791 if ts-two-column-body.get() { span(content) } else { content }
792}
793
794#let frontmatter-colophon(body) = context {
795 let u = text.size
796 let content = block(
797 above: u * 3, width: 26em,
798 inset: (top: u),
799 stroke: (top: 0.5pt + rule-color),
800 {
801 set text(size: u * 0.86, style: "italic", fill: ink-muted)
802 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
803 body
804 },
805 )
806 if ts-two-column-body.get() { span(content, at-bottom: true) } else { content }
807}
808
809// ── Letter ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
810
811// @s letter
812// A letter's page, and the letter's document setup: a deeper top margin than
813// foot or sides, so the sender block sits where an envelope window expects it,
814// and no running head or folio. A letter opens with this in place of
815// `#show: typeset` — the two cannot be stacked, because typeset() sets the page
816// and a page configuration underneath it sits inside a container, where Typst
817// refuses one.
818#let letter-page(
819 paper: "a4",
820 margin: (top: 32mm, bottom: 28mm, left: 25mm, right: 25mm),
821 doc,
822) = {
823 show: typeset.with(
824 paper: paper,
825 margin: margin,
826 running-head: false,
827 folio: false,
828 )
829 doc
830}
831// @e
832
833// The sender block is address data, not a masthead: one style throughout, at
834// body size, in the reading face. Nothing bold, nothing in the sans.
835#let letter-sender(body) = context {
836 let u = text.size
837 block(below: u * 2.5, {
838 set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.35), first-line-indent: 0pt)
839 body
840 })
841}
842
843// A line under the date — a dedication, a feast, a devotion. It belongs to the
844// date, so it takes no gap of its own.
845#let letter-date-note(body) = context {
846 let u = text.size
847 block(above: 0.1em, below: u * 1.5, {
848 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
849 text(style: "italic", body)
850 })
851}
852
853#let letter-address-block(label: none, body) = block(below: sp * 1.5, {
854 set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.35), first-line-indent: 0pt)
855 if label != none {
856 block(below: 0.25em, text(font: sans, size: xs, tracking: 0.1em, fill: ink-faint, upper(label)))
857 }
858 body
859})
860
861// The typed name, with room above it to sign. No rule: a ruled line is a form
862// to be filled in, and this is a letter.
863#let letter-signature(name) = context {
864 let u = text.size
865 block(above: u * 3, breakable: false, {
866 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
867 name
868 })
869}
870
871// "Enc." introduces a sentence; it does not head a section.
872#let letter-enclosures(body) = context {
873 let u = text.size
874 block(above: u * 2, {
875 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
876 [Enc. ]
877 body
878 })
879}
880
881// A postscript is a sentence that happens to begin with "P.S." — the label is
882// not a heading, so it matches the text it introduces exactly.
883#let letter-postscript(body) = context {
884 let u = text.size
885 block(above: u, {
886 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
887 [P.S. ]
888 body
889 })
890}
891
892// ── Apparatus ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
893
894// @s toc
895#let toc() = {
896 show outline.entry: set text(font: sans, size: sm)
897 set outline.entry(fill: repeat(gap: 0.4em)[.])
898 outline(title: none, indent: 1.5em)
899}
900// @e
901
902// @s notes
903// Anchored past the text column's right edge. In Typst the column width is
904// explicit (the `measure` argument), so the offset is taken from it directly.
905#let notes-sidenote(body) = place(
906 right,
907 dx: 13em,
908 dy: -0.3em,
909 block(width: 11em, {
910 set text(font: sans, size: xs, fill: ink-muted)
911 set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.4), first-line-indent: 0pt)
912 body
913 }),
914)
915// @e
916
917// ── Utilities ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
918
919// @s utilities
920#let utilities-keep-together(body) = block(breakable: false, body)
921#let utilities-tie(body) = box(body)
922// @e
